messages.content: Estou planejando um acampamento e preciso saber a previsão do tempo. Você pode me buscar os dados meteorológicos do acampamento localizado para os próximos 10 dias, incluindo previsões diárias de temperatura e precipitação? Além disso, prefiro a temperatura máxima de 2 minutos em Fahrenheit e a soma da precipitação em polegadas.

function.name: requests_get
function.description: Sends a GET request to the specified URL to retrieve weather data from the Open-Meteo API. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

url.description: URL of the Open-Meteo API endpoint.

headers.description: Headers to include in the request. Each key-value pair represents a header field and its value.

Content-Type.description: The MIME type of the body of the request (used with POST and PUT requests).

Accept.description: Media type(s) that is/are acceptable for the response.

timeout.description: Maximum time in seconds to wait for the server to send data before giving up. This is a float type value.

params.description: Query parameters for the GET request.

latitude.description: Latitude of the location, positive for N and negative for S. This is a float type value.

longitude.description: Longitude of the location, positive for E and negative for W. This is a float type value.

elevation.description: Elevation in meters above sea level for the location. The default value represents no elevation downscaling.

auth.description: Authentication tuple for HTTP authentication, in the format (username, password).

cert.description: Path to the SSL client certificate file (.pem). A null value means no client certificate is used.

cookies.description: Dictionary of cookies to send with the request. Each key represents a cookie name.

proxies.description: Dictionary mapping protocol names to the URL of the proxy. Each key-value pair represents a protocol and its proxy URL.

stream.description: If True, the response should be streamed; otherwise, it should be downloaded immediately.

verify.description: Whether to verify the server's TLS certificate.

message.content:
Para obter a previsão do tempo correta, preciso saber a localização exata do acampamento. Você pode me informar a latitude e longitude (ou a cidade/estado mais próximo) onde o acampamento será realizado?

Além disso, você mencionou “temperatura máxima de 2 minutos”. Poderia esclarecer se você quer a temperatura máxima às 2 h da manhã, às 2 h da tarde, ou algo diferente? Assim poderei configurar a consulta corretamente.

Assim que eu tiver esses detalhes, farei a chamada à API do Open‑Meteo e retornarei:

- Previsão diária de temperatura máxima (em °F) e precipitação (em polegadas) para os próximos 10 dias.
- Soma total da precipitação em polegadas para esse período.
message.reasoning: The user wants weather forecast for a camping location for next 10 days, including daily temperature and precipitation. They prefer maximum temperature of 2 minutes in Fahrenheit and sum of precipitation in inches. They didn't specify location coordinates. We need to ask for location. Also they want "maximum temperature of 2 minutes" - maybe they mean "max temperature at 2am"? But they wrote "máxima de 2 minutos". Might be a mistake. They want max temperature at 2 minutes? That doesn't make sense. Maybe they want "max temperature at 2am" or "max temperature at 2pm"? But they wrote "máxima de 2 minutos". Could be "max temperature at 2am" but they wrote "2 minutos". Could be "2am" but they wrote "2 minutos". Let's interpret as "max temperature at 2am" or "max temperature at 2pm"? Actually "máxima de 2 minutos" might be "max temperature at 2am" because 2 minutes after midnight? But typical forecast times are hourly. They might want "max temperature at 2am" but that is weird. They might want "max temperature at 2pm" but they wrote "2 minutos". Could be a typo. We can ask clarifying question: "Você poderia me informar a localização exata (latitude e longitude) do acampamento?" Also clarify "Você quis dizer temperatura máxima às 2h da manhã ou 2h da tarde?" Also ask if they want precipitation sum in inches. We can provide the forecast once we have location. So we need to ask for location.
